units.one_line: Owns EVM connection and chain settings, including ingestion defaults, without node profiles, file loading or provider I/O.

key_types.name: ChainConfig
key_types.what: one chain: endpoint, authentication, configured contracts, finalization, ingestion and data-availability settings

key_types.name: ContractAddresses
key_types.what: named configured contract endpoints, not checked ABI bindings or verified chain facts

key_types.name: Contract
key_types.what: a bare address or an address with its deployment block

key_types.name: RPC
key_types.what: validated HTTP(S)/WS(S) endpoint with protocol conversion and locality helpers

key_types.name: RpcAuth
key_types.what: none, basic credentials or a bearer token, using the configuration serde representation

read_first.why: production-safe ingestion defaults and explicit overrides

rust_patterns.note: untagged serde accepts a contract address string or a table with deploy_block

units.tests: Run cargo test --locked -p e3-evm-config for endpoint handling and ingestion defaults/validation; CLI and runtime tests cover the consumers.
unverified: Settings validation does not establish chain identity, canonical history or exactly-once effects.

units.one_line: Shares the EVM transaction rules of client, runtime and CLI senders: receipt success, nonce choice, broadcast refusal and RPC retry classification, without their locks or attempt policies.

key_types.name: RevertedTransaction
key_types.what: a mined transaction whose receipt reports execution failure, with its operation and hash

read_first.why: the crate entry: the shared rules and what callers keep
the nonce choice from local reservations and the RPC pending count
which failed broadcasts free their nonce
a receipt check, so that RPC submission is not taken for success

rust_patterns.note: broadcast_refused matches the alloy contract and RPC error variants

units.tests: Run cargo test --locked -p e3-evm-transactions for receipt status, nonce reservation and expiry, and broadcast-refusal classification; the client and runtime tests cover their lock and retry wrappers.
unverified: The broadcast-refusal messages are matched as text; other node implementations can word an already-known answer differently.

units.one_line: Shared checked Solidity ABI bindings, independent of node and application delivery policies.
units.tests: Run pnpm evm:build and pnpm check:bindings, then cargo test --locked -p e3-evm-contracts.

units.one_line: Content-addressed object transport and pure committee-key chunk mechanics; admission and recovery stay with callers.

state.name: Object bytes (at most 1 MiB) carried by Avail submit_data extrinsics

key_types.name: DataReference
key_types.what: content hash, Avail block number, and leaf index that Ethereum records for one object

key_types.name: PendingPublication
key_types.what: Avail block hash, block number, and extrinsic index needed to request a bridge proof

key_types.name: ProofStatus
key_types.what: Pending, or Ready with the ABI-encoded Merkle proof and the reference

key_types.name: VectorXBridgeApi
key_types.what: HTTP client for the official Avail VectorX bridge proof route

key_types.name: AvailPublisher
key_types.what: signs submit_data, waits for finality, and returns the coordinates needed for the proof

key_types.name: AvailReader
key_types.what: finds the submit_data call with the matching content hash in the Ethereum-verified block

key_types.name: HttpObjectReader
key_types.what: mock reader: GET /objects/0x<hash> from a local HTTP server

key_types.name: ChunkLayout
key_types.what: ephemeral public-key chunk layout, independent of consumer persistence and key authority

read_first.why: crate purpose and the trust split: receipt on chain, re-hash on read
the retrieval boundary that the e3-evm coordinator calls
the hash check that every reader runs before it returns bytes
publish path: submit, wait for finality, return the coordinates

rust_patterns.note: async trait with Send and Sync bounds; the Avail reader and the HTTP mock reader implement it
the HTTP reader's retrieve() re-hashes the bytes before it returns them
size and emptiness are checked before the bytes are hashed
a bad bridge URL reports a human-readable context
DataReference derives serde, so it can be serialized
rust_patterns.ref: crates/data-availability/src/lib.rs@29@#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]

rust_patterns.note: the re-hash rule is tested offline: matching bytes pass, substituted bytes fail

units.tests: cargo test -p e3-data-availability. Add --features avail-read to also run the Avail module test (avail.rs is gated in lib.rs).
unverified: Live Avail and VectorX behaviour was not exercised; the proof shape is covered only by the offline tests in lib.rs.
